plants.name: Colchicum autumnale
plants.description: Goblet-shaped lilac-pink blooms rise straight out of bare ground on slender white stalks. The leaves are long gone, so the flowers look like they have appeared by magic. They scatter color across damp meadows and woodland edges just as autumn begins.
plants.bloomingSeason: August to November, with a peak in September and October
plants.location: Meadows and grassy woodland in central and southern Europe, widely naturalised in northern Europe
plants.funFact: Autumn crocus flowers in autumn but sets its leaves and seed capsule in spring. This earns it the nickname 'naked ladies'. It is also the source of colchicine, a compound used in medicine and in plant breeding. The whole plant is highly toxic.

plants.name: Symphyotrichum novae-angliae
plants.description: Dense clusters of daisy-like flowers with narrow violet-purple petals around golden-yellow centers. They light up roadsides, prairies and garden borders when most other blooms are fading. Bees and migrating butterflies gather on them in large numbers.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer to autumn, roughly August through October
plants.location: Eastern and central North America, in meadows, prairies and garden borders
plants.funFact: New England asters are a key fuel stop for migrating monarch butterflies. The flower heads close up on dull, cloudy days and open again in sunshine.

plants.name: Cosmos bipinnatus
plants.description: Airy, feathery foliage carries saucer-shaped blooms that sway on tall, slender stems. They are cheerful and easy to grow, and they keep producing flowers until the first hard frosts arrive. They are a favorite in cottage gardens and cutting beds.
plants.bloomingSeason: Summer through autumn, roughly June to October in temperate northern gardens
plants.location: Temperate Northern Hemisphere gardens, such as the American Midwest; native to Mexico
plants.funFact: Cosmos comes from a Greek word meaning 'order' or 'harmony', a nod to the tidy, balanced arrangement of its petals. Regular deadheading keeps the plants blooming for months.
